set.request: devbar's draggable edge intercepts scrollbar user input.
steps: Measure the overlap in the live tab
Get the target-size decision from Mike
Move the grip inside the rail (grip.css)
Drop the --dev-grip term from the closed slide (devbar.css)
Verify: scrollbar draggable, grip still resizes, closed rail still clear
Refresh the docs that record the straddle
set.outcome: **The page's scrollbar is reachable again.** `.pages` is `overflow-y: scroll`, so the page region always reserves a scroll gutter flush against the rail's inline-start edge — exactly where `.dev-grip` straddled at `2rem` wide. Measured on /framework/ext/Panel/ at 2706: gutter 1931→1946, grip 1931→1963, `elementFromPoint` returning `dev-grip` for every pixel of the scrollbar, with `setPointerCapture` swallowing the whole drag. There is no room on the page side of that line at all, so the grip moved wholly inside the rail: `--dev-grip: 2rem` + `translateX(-50%)` became a plain `width: 0.75rem`, landing on the dead strip the rail already had (1px border + 0.9em padding on head/tabs/body), so no content moved. Two things fell out: `devbar.css` hides with a plain `translateX(100%)` again and the `--dev-grip` token is gone, so the two files can no longer disagree about a number they no longer share. Verified — real Chrome: overlap 0px, every gutter probe returns `pages`; closed grip 2707→2719, off screen. Headless 1600 with a real mouse: the grip drag took the rail 300→420 following the pointer exactly. Cost, recorded: a 12px target where the straddle offered 32. Docs refreshed: readme.md (a new Decision + an Open note), doc/docking.md, doc/file/grip.css.md, doc/file/devbar.css.md, doc/file/grip.js.md, and four now-false comments in grip.css, grip.js and DevBar.js. All eight DevBar doc urls load clean at 1600 — no console errors, no md-error, no overflow.
